description: Version 2.3 (gripper plus handles; builds on 2.2, related pebble voice-f7f729ac). Jake: 2.2 looks more like what we want. Keep the 2.2 handles but drop the little connector. Instead the handle piece should slide into the gripper: there is a little hook at the very base of the gripper, between where the gripper tip starts to round out and the base. Give the handle a long, narrow tongue (quite long, not so wide) that slides in from the top into a matching pocket/channel running along the flat face of the gripper near that base hook.

results.identified_issue: Interpretation: 'connector' = 2.2's yellow lug; 'flat face' = the finger's outer edge face (the face 2.2's plate is flush to, which Jake liked); 'hook at the base' = the J-hook whose notch (rail frame u -11.4..-9.2, w 0..4.3) opens toward the tip; 'from the top' = sliding along u toward the base. A straight dovetail can't be open at its top end without running the full finger edge, so the pocket is a keyhole (lips u -9.4..-0.8, head-wide window above, 1 mm-deep bar slot to u 22.6) and the handle slides slide_len_in=8.4 mm. Plate inboard face at w 0.45; foot trimmed by offset(r=fit) profile(). Holes come within 1-1.9 mm of the outer edge, so the 2.2 mm pocket breaches 4 of them (genus 37 = 33+4, BREACHED in genus.py). Rejected: pocket in the dorsal honeycomb face (breaches far more holes); plain slot with no undercut (handle pivots out about the hook). Cutters overlap by 0.05 mm to avoid CGAL non-manifold seams. All checks pass (export, genus, check_geometry incl. new insertion and retention checks, render_compare 97-100%, test_gripper_poses, test_publish_designs). Not printed; the window roof is a 2.25 mm unsupported overhang when the finger prints flat.
results.summary: Made version 2.3: the yellow connector block is gone. Each 2.2 handle now has a long, narrow tongue that slides down from the top into a pocket in the finger's outer edge, and its foot tucks behind the base hook.
results.detailed_description:
New folder v203_generalist_tongue_pocket is 2.2 with the yellow lug removed. The black handle is the same plate as 2.2 (28 × 37 mm, two strap slots). It now sits right against the finger's outer edge, and its bottom end drops into the little hook's notch at the base.

On its inner face is a tongue 23 mm long and 3.5 mm wide. The finger has a matching pocket running up the outer edge from the hook. The pocket is a keyhole. The bottom 8 mm of the tongue is a dovetail head. You drop the head into a wider window in the pocket, then slide the handle about 8 mm down toward the hook. The head then sits under the pocket's lips, and the handle's foot sits behind the hook. Together they keep it from pulling outward. Only friction stops it sliding back up, same as 2.2.

Heads-up: the finger's edge is thin there, so the pocket cuts into the sides of 4 honeycomb holes near the edge. They still go all the way through. All checks pass, including the fit, the retention, a clean slide-in from the window, and the fingers' contact. Nothing is printed yet. If you pictured the pocket on the big honeycomb face instead of the outer edge, or a plain slot with no dovetail, tell me.

summary: The gripper-and-handle design in version 2.3 should keep the 2.2 handles but drop the small connector between the two parts. The handle should instead get a long, narrow tongue that slides in from the top into a matching pocket along the gripper's flat face near the base hook.
